result:
Summary: The Transformer architecture has fundamentally reshaped the landscape of natural language processing by enabling each token in a sequence to attend to every other token simultaneously, but this powerful capability comes with the well-documented 𝒪(n²) computational complexity with respect to the sequence length nn. In a standard Transformer network, each of the nn tokens in a sequence computes pairwise interactions (queries, keys, and values) with every other token, leading to both computational and memory requirements that scale quadratically with the sequence length. This quadratic dependence on n poses a challenge for very long input sequences, both from the training and testing perspectives.
